items.title: What Your Machine Actually Needs to Run a Local AI Engineering Team
items.teaser: Neural Junkie ships as a ~15 MB desktop app — but your first local model pull can be 14 GB+. Here is how RAM tiers map to model tags, why multi-agent ≠ multi-model, and what we do not hide in open beta.

items.title: We Don't Use One Model. We Layer Them.
items.teaser: One 14B model can't be your security reviewer, biology expert, session summarizer, and cheap typo-fixer. Neural Junkie layers models at four levels — context, weights, routing, and orchestration — so local multi-agent work stays fast, grounded, and under your control.

items.title: Modular AI, Local Hardware: How Neural Junkie Routes Instead of Guessing
items.teaser: Stop running one model for everything. Neural Junkie composes specialists at the orchestration layer — a small classifier picks domain and cost tier, packs declare chat/tool/LoRA stacks, and every reply shows which model actually ran.

items.title: Decide Before You Generate: Neural Junkie's Inference Layer
items.teaser: Everyone optimizes inference speed. Almost nobody optimizes inference *avoidance*. Neural Junkie's inference layer decides whether to call a model, which brain to use, and which provider runs the job — then shows you the answer on the message itself.

items.title: We Didn't Build One Agent Loop. We Built a Stack.
items.teaser: My agent could run `make start-all` eight times and never touch the Makefile. That's not a model problem — it's a missing closed loop. Here's the stack of loops we built in Neural Junkie, and why each one exists.

items.title: Execution Is Not Repair: Building the NJ Fix Loop
items.teaser: My agent could run `make start-all` eight times and never touch the Makefile. Execution worked; repair didn't. Here's the platform policy we added so boot-fix sessions read, edit, verify, and always report an outcome.

items.title: Build the IDE You Actually Own
items.teaser: IDE v4 adds Monaco LSP, remote SSH via nj-remote, dev containers, and tree-sitter symbols — local-first and open source, for when the IDE you loved has a new owner.

items.title: Your Agents Forget. Neural Junkie Remembers — Without Sending the Whole Transcript.
items.teaser: Neural Junkie agents used to forget anything outside the last few messages. Conversation memory indexes your full channel history and collab artifacts locally, then pulls back only what's relevant to your latest question — no cloud vector DB, no stuffing the whole transcript into context.

items.title: One Base Model. Many Specialists. LoRA Inside Neural Junkie.
items.teaser: Running five local specialists shouldn’t mean five full 14B downloads. Neural Junkie composes Ollama tags from one base + small LoRA adapters — import from Hugging Face, install pack presets, or train from your own chat and collab history.

items.title: Why We Split Inference and LoRA Into Two Tiers
items.teaser: We wanted one Qwen base + tiny LoRA adapters for every specialist. Ollama said no — safetensors LoRA only works on Llama/Mistral/Gemma. Here's how Neural Junkie split inference (Qwen) from train/compose (Llama) without breaking the hub.

items.title: Two Layers, One Specialist: MCP Exports and LoRA in Neural Junkie
items.teaser: Repo experts accumulate real value — indexed code, session Q&A, architecture notes. We export that as portable MCP packages *and* optionally fine-tune LoRA adapters from the same sessions. Same ambition, different layer: context you can share vs weights that lean local inference toward your domain.

items.title: Multi-Agent Collaboration Is Easy to Demo. Hard to Ship.
items.teaser: `/collaborate` looks like one command. Under the hood it’s phases, task dependencies, workspace gates, and file approvals — while real models improvise. Here’s why that’s hard, and the three-layer test harness I’m building so it doesn’t stay a demo.

items.title: You Can’t Unit Test a Conversation. So I Built This Instead.
items.teaser: Prompts and models change weekly. Click-testing a multi-agent hub doesn’t scale. Here’s the three-layer harness I built for Neural Junkie — deterministic Go tests for the orchestrator, CI smoke for the pipeline, and JSON scenarios with real Ollama agents for conversation quality.
